Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:3:description: When iterative codex review (or similar adversarial reviewer) keeps surfacing finer-grained concerns on the same logical surface, decide disposition by confidence trend AND severity gate. Monotone-decline + low/medium severity → ACCEPT-WITH-DOC. Escalation OR unresolved high/critical → REVERT-AND-REMOVE. Owner-accepted high/critical → MANUAL-OVERRIDE (distinct, tracked). Stop the arc at round 5 regardless.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:29:**Critical**: stopping iteration is independent of shipping disposition. Hitting round 5 does NOT mean the surface is safe to ship — it means you've spent enough effort on layer-fix and need to switch to a terminal disposition (ACCEPT-WITH-DOC, REVERT-AND-REMOVE, or escalate to user). The terminal disposition has its OWN gates beyond iteration count.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:35:### Severity gate (mandatory before ACCEPT-WITH-DOC)
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:37:ACCEPT-WITH-DOC is a **hard deny** for any unresolved `high` or `critical` codex severity. No combination of confidence trend, iteration count, or owner signoff can convert an unresolved high/critical finding into ACCEPT-WITH-DOC. (If you want to ship anyway, see the separate MANUAL-OVERRIDE disposition below.)
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:39:For findings at `medium` or `low` severity, ACCEPT-WITH-DOC additionally requires AT LEAST ONE of:
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:46:### Outcome A — ACCEPT-WITH-DOC (monotone-decline AND severity-gate satisfied)
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:57:Disposition: ship a doc-comment ACCEPT in the patch site explaining threat model + verification reference + ROI + upstream issue queue. Future workers see the explicit acceptance; arc closes cleanly.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:59:**Anti-example (would FAIL the severity gate)**: round 1 high (0.88) → round 2 high (0.80) → round 3 high (0.73) → "stop at round 5 ceiling, monotone-decline, ACCEPT". This would be wrong — severity stayed high; the underlying defect is still material; ACCEPT-WITH-DOC normalizes shipping known security/correctness regressions.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:63:Confidence reverses between rounds on the **same concern**. This is codex saying "your disposition didn't address my actual point" — an ACCEPT comment doesn't fix a security bug, and codex is escalating to ensure you don't ship the unfixed surface.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:68:Round 3: 0.86 (escalation — ACCEPT was wrong)
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:75:When ACCEPT-WITH-DOC's hard-deny on high/critical blocks shipping but the user or named risk-owner explicitly wants the work to land anyway, this is a SEPARATE disposition — not ACCEPT. Future readers must be able to grep for "we shipped a known high/critical defect with explicit acceptance" without that being conflated with "we did our due diligence and bounded the residual risk."
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:79:The separation matters because conflating MANUAL-OVERRIDE with ACCEPT lets future commits silently bless known material defects.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:86:- **Confuse ACCEPT with convergence**: shipping an ACCEPT comment on an escalating concern produces *worse* documentation than just removing the feature, because future readers see "we knew this was broken and shipped it anyway"
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:87:- **Burn the closed-loop discipline**: codex's value comes from being adversarial; if you keep ACCEPT'ing without checking the confidence trend, you train yourself to ignore real findings
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:103:3. **ACCEPT-WITH-DOC** ONLY if: last-round severity is `medium` or lower AND severity gate passes (concrete verification OR severity downgrade in evidence) AND confidence declined monotonically. Hard deny for any unresolved `high`/`critical`.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:104:4. **MANUAL-OVERRIDE** if: user/owner explicitly accepts unresolved high/critical risk for this specific commit. Distinct from ACCEPT — uses `MANUAL-OVERRIDE` marker, tracked as code-review-burn metric.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:107:## Anti-pattern: ACCEPT-WITH-DOC on escalating concern
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:109:When an arc reaches a late round (e.g., round 28+) and the threat model is offered as bounding the risk, watch the trend rather than the framing. If the next round still ESCALATES (e.g., 0.78 → 0.86) because the threat model isn't enforced in code, codex is correctly noting the failure mode remains silent and user-visible only after data has been exfiltrated. The ACCEPT comment didn't address the actual concern; it documented a known-broken state.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:111:Lesson: ACCEPT-WITH-DOC is only valid when codex's confidence trend confirms convergence. Watch the trend, not just the current round.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:115:Outcome B (REVERT-AND-REMOVE) is not necessarily terminal for the underlying work. A common recovery shape is: REVERT removes the over-broad surface → a later, narrower fix-forward re-introduces the work with the invariant preserved + scope bounded → that narrower fix-forward converges via Outcome A (monotone-decline ACCEPT). Track the two as separate arcs (the REVERT closes arc 1; the narrower re-introduction opens arc 2) rather than as a single iteration.

Cite class downgraded to TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL with REQUIRED metadata: (a) ISBN/DOI + page + verbatim-quote inline; (b) verifier-identity disclosure (who-verified-when, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-04 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`); (c) explicit `non-automatable: true` marker so review hooks know to defer to human sign-off; (d) **HARD-GATE ELIGIBILITY TEST** *(Round-3 amendment a per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "MUST prefer" soft preference framing — preference is not gateable; eligibility is)*: PROVISIONAL admission is admissible ONLY when DOI landing page + accessible PDF / publisher excerpt / archived scan (license-permitting) was SEARCHED AND UNAVAILABLE. The commit body MUST document the search (which DOI/publisher/archive was queried + return shape — e.g., "searched ACM DOI 10.1145/<doi> 2026-05-05 — paywall-only, no excerpt found; searched Internet Archive — no scan; searched publisher excerpt page — none"). Mere preference is INSUFFICIENT — if any auditable surrogate exists (DOI/PDF/excerpt/scan), use it as the normative source instead of the physical-only book cite. e.g., ACM DOI `https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/<doi>` for ACM papers IS auditable when paywall-free. Z:\claude-sota-installed\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:18:    3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Z:\claude-sota-installed\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:20:    4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.
Z:\claude-sota-installed\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:22:    5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.

  32: # Codification threshold
  33: 
  34: Codify a newly-observed pattern as reference memory (or rule) at **n=1** IF all of:
  35: 
  36: 1. Expected savings = `re-derive cost × frequency` > ~10 minutes/month [REVISED parent-cycle-321 from original `cost > 15 min AND freq ≥ 1/mo` separate-gate check]
  37: 2. Codification artifact fits bounded-ship 200-LOC ceiling (parent `reference_bounded_ship_per_loop_fire.md` cycle-300 — FORWARD-REF until sss memory port)
  38: 
  39: Otherwise defer until **n=2** confirmation.
  40: 
  41: ## Jurisdiction — trigger-type matters, not file prefix [ADDED parent-cycle-322]
  42: 
  43: This rule applies to **self-observed** pattern codifications — cases where the harness (you/Claude) notices a recurring issue / edge case / methodology via live-probe failure, audit finding, or inter-cycle observation, and decides whether to record it.
  44: 
  45: This rule does **NOT** apply to **user-triggered** codifications — cases where the user issues an explicit signal (correction: "no, don't do X"; confirmation: "yes exactly, keep doing that"; standing directive: "always do Y"). User-triggered codifications default to **n=1 always** per the auto-memory system-prompt's feedback-trigger semantics — the user's signal IS the signal to record.
  46: 
  47: **Critical**: the distinction is trigger-type, NOT file-prefix. The `feedback_` / `reference_` / `project_` prefix naming is an organizational convention; it does NOT tell you whether the codification was user-triggered or self-observed. Examples (PARENT-ATTRIBUTION):
  48: 
  49: - `feedback_mid_session_env_propagation.md` (parent cycle-296) — filed under `feedback_` prefix but was self-observed via live-probe failure, no user quote. **Subject to this rule** — and correctly included in the cycle-321 evidence trio.
  50: - `feedback_audit_high_quality_source_bias.md` — filed under `feedback_` prefix AND user-triggered (explicit Round-23 user quote). **NOT subject to this rule** — n=1 was automatic.
  51: - `reference_post_arc_adoption_subchain.md` (parent cycle-318) — filed under `reference_` prefix, self-observed from 4-cycle Cognee arc. **Subject to this rule**.
  52: 
  53: Before applying steps 1-3 below, first classify the codification's trigger. If user-triggered, skip this rule entirely and codify at n=1.
  54: 
  55: ## Why this rule exists
  56: 
  57: The prior default was "wait for n≥2 before codifying" (parent cycle-273 close report), which protected against over-specification from small samples. But three consecutive n=1 codifications (parent cycle-296, 318, 319) have all held against subsequent applications without revision — the n≥2 bar was a proxy for "avoid premature codification" when the root metric is **cost-per-miss**.
  58: 
  59: Codifying too early costs LOC in a reference file (~50-150 LOC typical). Codifying too late costs re-derive time at each future application. For patterns where re-derive is cheap (~minutes), waiting for n=2 is effectively free. For patterns where re-derive is expensive (>15 min), every "wait for n=2" burns 15+ min on the next application — and if frequency is several per month, the wait dominates.
  60: 
  61: ## Evidence trio (PARENT-ATTRIBUTION)
  62: 
  63: | Cycle | Pattern | Re-derive cost per miss | Frequency expected | Codified at n | Held against later applications? |
  64: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  65: | 296 | Mid-session env non-propagation | ~30 min (debug phantom failure) | 1-2 per arc | 1 | YES — applied cycles 298/299/303/306/316 without revision |
  66: | 318 | 4-cycle post-arc adoption subchain | ~30-45 min (re-derive 4-step structure) | ~1-2 per month | 1 | YES so far — cycle-319 cascaded-corrected one phrasing, structure unchanged |
  67: | 319 | GGUF-via-Ollama Probe-3 gatekeeper variant | ~15-20 min × ~3-5/mo = 45-100 min/mo | ~3-5 per month (Devstral / Qwen3.6 / Gemma4 quants) | 1 | Pending n=2 |
  68: 
  69: ## How to apply
  70: 
  71: Before deciding whether to codify a newly-observed pattern:
  72: 
  73: 1. **Estimate re-derive cost.** How long for a future-you (no memory of this cycle) to reconstruct the pattern from primary evidence? Include reading source files, running probes, debugging dead-ends.
  74: 2. **Estimate future application frequency.** How often will this pattern surface in the next 1-3 months? Count conservatively — unrealized frequency inflates false savings.
  75: 3. **Size the codification.** Will it fit under the 200-LOC bounded-ship ceiling? If not, split into sub-patterns and codify the smallest recurring unit.
  76: 4. **Decision [REVISED parent-cycle-321 per `reports/cycle-321-codification-threshold-audit-2026-04-23.md` — PARENT-ATTRIBUTION]:**
  77:    - Compute `expected savings = re-derive cost × frequency` (min/month). Breakeven ~10 min/month (implied LOC-read cost ~1-2 min × future readers).
  78:    - `expected savings > ~10 min/month` AND `LOC ≤ 200` → codify NOW at n=1
  79:    - `expected savings ≤ ~10 min/month` → defer until n=2 confirmation
  80:    - `LOC > 200` → split into sub-patterns first, then apply steps 1-3 to each
  81:    - Prior gate (parent cycle-320 original) used `cost > 15 min AND freq ≥ 1/month` independently, which rejected high-frequency low-per-miss patterns like `reference_wave_report_cascaded_correction.md` (10 min × ~16/mo = 160 min/mo savings — clear PASS under revised gate, FAIL under original). See parent audit report for full analysis.
  82: 5. **Mark the codification** with rationale: `n=1 per .claude/rules/codification-threshold.md — expected savings = ~X min × ~Y/mo = Z min/mo`. At n=2 (next application), explicitly re-evaluate: confirm / revise / retract.
